record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: Given a finite set consisting of three polyominoes, or alternatively four polyominoes, is the problem of deciding whether that set tiles the plane undecidable?

evidence.quote: Ollinger [31] proved that determining whether a set of 5 polyominoes tile the plane is undecidable
The existence of aperiodic sets of three polyominoes opens possibility that determining whether a set of just three or four polyominoes has a tiling is undecidable
Open Problem 9 (Open Problem 2 of [31]) Is determining whether a set of three (or four) polyominoes tile the plane undecidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a finite, edge-connected union of unit squares of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. A finite set $S = \{P_1, \dots, P_k\}$ of polyominoes is said to tile the plane if there exists a covering of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by interior-disjoint copies of the $P_i$, where each copy is obtained from some $P_i$ by a translation, rotation, and/or reflection (and every $P_i$ may be used arbitrarily many times). The polyomino tiling problem with $k$ tiles asks: given as input a finite set $S$ of $k$ polyominoes (specified by their unit-square coordinates), decide whether $S$ tiles the plane.

It is known that this decision problem is undecidable for $k = 5$. Determine whether the polyomino tiling problem is undecidable when $k = 3$, and whether it is undecidable when $k = 4$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent progress has tightened the undecidability bound for polyomino tilings: Yang–Zhang proved undecidability for translational tiling with 8 polyominoes (2024), and a 2025 preprint establishes undecidability for sets of 5 polyominoes. For general simple polygons, Demaine–Langerman (SoCG 2025) proved undecidability with 3 prototiles, but this concerns polygons, not polyominoes. The cases of 3 or 4 polyominoes appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability of tiling the plane with a set of 5 polyominoes
status_evidence.snippet: Undecidability of Tiling the Plane with a Set of 5 Polyominoes
status_evidence.claim: State of the art for polyominoes is 5; smaller k (3 or 4) not addressed.

status_evidence.title: A proof of Ollinger's conjecture: undecidability of tiling the plane with a set of 8 polyominoes
status_evidence.snippet: undecidability of tiling the plane with translated copies of a set of 8 polyominoes
status_evidence.claim: Best translational-tiling bound for polyominoes is 8.

status_evidence.title: Tiling with Three Polygons is Undecidable
status_evidence.snippet: Given three simple-polygon prototiles, determining whether they tile the plane is undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: The 3-prototile result applies to general polygons, not polyominoes.
